answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate and 14-day contract expiration create urgency, but the 94% volume commitment eliminates switching risk tolerance. Memory_c4 demonstrated that benchmarking recovered real margin at renewal; memory_c6 showed multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing; memory_c2 confirmed the low-cost vendor exists but switching carries onboarding friction. Rather than commit to renew (locking in current rates) or switch (introducing delivery risk during peak utilization), aggressive renegotiation using market benchmarks offers margin recovery without operational disruption. Verifying memory_c4's benchmarking approach will confirm the leverage framework. This preserves optionality: if negotiation fails, renewal remains available within the 14-day window. The constraint is real—18% cut forces action—but staged negotiation buys information about incumbent flexibility before capacity decisions lock in.
